title: Three letters, then a hard question.
subtitle: Pausing before a surah about tests

row.title: a question
sub: do you think you will not be tested?

key.label: What the letters ask of you

then: This surah came in Makkah during {trap}heavy persecution of the early Muslims.{/trap} It opens with three letters whose meaning is known to Allah. Ibn Kathir does not explain them here. He points straight to what follows: {idea}a question about tests.{/idea}
now: You open the app on the bus, half tired, thumb ready to scroll. Three letters you cannot translate sit at the top. {idea}They slow you down.{/idea} Before you hear the hard question, you are asked to be present for it.
old: If I cannot understand a word, I can skip it.
new: Some words are there to make me stop, so I hear what comes next properly.
try: Before reading the next verse, put the phone down for three breaths and then read it slowly.

title: Saying I believe opens the test, not ends it.
subtitle: Why faith is always tried
then: The early Muslims of Makkah were being beaten, boycotted and mocked. The verse is {idea}a rebuke in the form of a question.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that the people most tested are the Prophets, then the righteous, then the next best, {reward}each by the strength of his faith.{/reward}
now: You started praying on time this month. Then work got crushing, your sleep broke, and a family argument flared. {trap}It feels like it went wrong because you tried.{/trap} The verse says this is the normal shape of the road. {idea}The test is how claims become real.{/idea}
old: If I am sincere, things should get easier.
new: Being tested is not a sign that Allah left me. It is how my faith is shown to be true.
try: Name one hard thing in your week and say, quietly, this is my test, not my punishment.

title: Every generation before you was tested too.
subtitle: Trials make the truthful and the liars evident

row.title: Allah finds out
sub: as if He did not know

row.title: it becomes evident
sub: He knew; now it is seen

then: The persecuted believers in Makkah were reminded that {reward}earlier believers had faced the same.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains that Allah already knows everything, past and future. The test makes {idea}who is sincere and who is lying{/idea} visible in the real world.
now: You read about your grandparents leaving a home with almost nothing, holding on to their prayers. Now your test is smaller, a boss who mocks your fasting, a friend group that drifts. {idea}Same line, new name in it.{/idea}
old: No one has had it as hard as me.
new: I am standing where believers have always stood, and the test only shows what is already in my heart.
try: Ask an older relative about one test they went through for their faith, and listen to the whole story.

title: No one outruns Allah.
subtitle: The wrongdoers' mistaken sense of escape

row.title: the wrongdoer
sub: no test seems to touch him

then: Believers were being tested while their oppressors seemed untouched. Ibn Kathir says those doing evil {trap}should not think they will escape{/trap} the trials, for a heavier reckoning lies ahead. {idea}Evil is what they judge.{/idea}
now: You see a colleague cut corners, take credit, and get promoted anyway. You start to wonder why you bother being honest. {trap}It looks like he got away with it.{/trap} The verse widens the frame. {idea}The story is not finished.{/idea}
old: People who do wrong and prosper have won.
new: No one slips past Allah. Delay is not escape, for them or for me.
try: Think of one small wrong you hoped nobody noticed. Fix it or ask forgiveness today.

title: The meeting you hope for is surely coming.
subtitle: Hope with a date on the calendar
then: To believers who were suffering, this was reassurance. Ibn Kathir says whoever hopes to meet Allah and does good will have {reward}his hopes fulfilled and his deeds rewarded in full.{/reward} It will surely come, because {idea}He hears all supplications and knows every need.{/idea}
now: You whisper a dua at night that nobody else knows about. You keep doing quiet good that no one thanks you for. {trap}It can feel like talking into the dark.{/trap} {idea}Someone hears, and the meeting is set.{/idea}
old: My quiet prayers and efforts probably go nowhere.
new: The One I hope to meet hears every word, and the meeting is certain.
try: Make one dua tonight for something you have stopped asking for.

title: Your striving is for you, not for Him.
subtitle: Allah does not need your effort
then: Believers in Makkah were paying a high price for their faith. Ibn Kathir explains that {reward}the benefit of every good deed comes back to the doer.{/reward} Even if everyone were as pious as the most pious person, {idea}it would add nothing to Allah's dominion.{/idea}
now: You wake for Fajr in a cold room and feel a bit proud, like you have given something. Or you resent it, like a tax. {idea}Neither is quite right.{/idea} The effort is building you. {reward}You are the one who walks away richer.{/reward}
old: My worship is something I give to Allah.
new: My worship is something Allah gives me the chance to gain from.
try: During one prayer today, think: this is for me, and thank Allah for letting me do it.

title: Your worst erased, your best rewarded.
subtitle: How generously Allah weighs deeds
then: Ibn Kathir notes that although Allah needs nothing, {idea}He is kind and generous.{/idea} He accepts the smallest good, multiplies one good deed from ten to seven hundred, and counts a bad deed as only one, {reward}or overlooks it entirely.{/reward}
now: You replay your worst moments at 2am, the shout at your kid, the lie at work. You assume that is who you are on the record. {idea}The verse promises a different accounting{/idea} for the one who believes and keeps doing good.
old: My bad days define me in Allah's eyes.
new: Allah wipes the misdeeds of those who believe and do good, and rewards them by their best.
try: Do one good deed today you would be glad to be judged by.

title: Be good to your parents, but not at Allah's expense.
subtitle: When love for family pulls against faith

row.title: his mother
sub: "I will not eat until you leave"

then: Families in Makkah pressed converts to return to the old religion, even using the Quran's own respect for parents as leverage. Sa'd said his mother refused food until he left Islam. {idea}This verse was revealed:{/idea} goodness to parents, but {trap}no obedience in associating partners with Allah.{/trap}
now: Your father wants you to skip prayer at the wedding so you do not "embarrass the family." Your mother says you are being extreme. {reward}You still owe them warmth and respect.{/reward} {idea}You do not owe them your faith.{/idea}
old: If I refuse my parents anything, I am a bad child.
new: I can be gentle and loyal to my parents and still keep Allah first.
try: Do one kind thing for a parent today, especially if you disagree with them about something.

title: You will be gathered with the righteous.
subtitle: The company you keep in the end
then: This follows the verse about parents who pushed their children away from Islam. Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}gathers the believer with the righteous,{/reward} not necessarily with his parents, even if he was closest to them in this world. {idea}A person is gathered with those he loves,{/idea} in faith.
now: You are the only one at the dinner table who prays. Sometimes you feel like the odd one out in your own family. {reward}The verse gives you a place to belong.{/reward} It promises you a company of good people at the end.
old: If my family does not share my faith, I am alone.
new: Allah places the believer among the righteous. I am not walking this alone.
try: Message one friend who helps you be better and tell them you are grateful for them.

title: When people hurt him, he thought Allah had.
subtitle: Faith that flips when the pressure comes
then: Some in Makkah claimed faith with their lips, but when hurt for it {trap}they treated people's harm like Allah's punishment{/trap} and left Islam, as Ibn 'Abbas explained. Yet when ease and gain came, they would say {trap}we were with you.{/trap} {idea}Allah knows what is in every heart.{/idea}
now: You are open about your faith until someone at work makes a joke about it. Then you go quiet, and later you hide it. When being Muslim becomes popular in your circle, you are suddenly loud again. {idea}Allah sees the whole pattern.{/idea}
old: When believing costs me, maybe it is a sign it was a mistake.
new: People's pressure is a trial, not Allah's verdict. My faith is shown by staying the same in both seasons.
try: Notice one place where you hide your faith out of fear, and take one small step to stop hiding it.

title: Hardship and ease both sort hearts.
subtitle: How the believer and the hypocrite are shown

row.title: obeys when it suits
sub: only when life goes my way

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah tests people {trap}with calamities{/trap} and {reward}with times of ease{/reward} to distinguish believers from hypocrites. The question is who obeys in both, and who obeys only {idea}when things go the way they want.{/idea}
now: Payday arrives with a bonus and suddenly you forget the duas you made when rent was due. Or a hospital visit makes you pray hard, then you drift once the scan is clear. {idea}Both seasons are the test.{/idea}
old: Tests only come when life gets hard.
new: Easy days test my heart as much as hard ones.
try: Thank Allah out loud today for one thing that is going well, before you ask for anything else.

title: No one can carry your sins for you.
subtitle: The empty promise: do it, I will take the blame

row.title: each carries his own
sub: no one lifts it for you

then: The disbelievers of Quraysh told the believers: leave your religion, follow our way, and {trap}we will bear your sins.{/trap} Ibn Kathir compares it to someone saying, do this and the sin is on my shoulders. Allah calls it a lie, for {idea}no soul bears another's burden.{/idea}
now: A friend says, "Just sign it, everyone does, if anything happens it is on me." A cousin says the same about a shady loan. {trap}It sounds generous.{/trap} {idea}But on the Day, your choices stay yours.{/idea}
old: If someone else talked me into it, the blame is theirs.
new: No one can take my sins off me, however confident they sound.
try: Next time someone says it is on me, pause and ask yourself if you would still do it alone.

title: Those who mislead carry extra loads.
subtitle: Influence adds to your burden or your reward
then: Ibn Kathir quotes the Sahih hadith: whoever calls to guidance gets {reward}a reward like those who follow him,{/reward} and whoever calls to misguidance carries {trap}a burden like those who follow him,{/trap} without reducing anyone's own share. They will also be questioned about the lies they invented.
now: You forward a cruel meme to the family group chat and twenty people pass it on. You teach your little brother a shortcut that is really cheating. {trap}Things you start keep traveling.{/trap} {reward}So do the good things.{/reward}
old: What others do after copying me is on them.
new: What I start, good or bad, keeps counting for me long after.
try: Share one thing today that you would be happy for a hundred people to copy.

title: Nuh called his people for 950 years.
subtitle: Patience longer than any lifetime

row.title: Nuh
sub: night and day, openly and secretly

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}consoled the Prophet ﷺ{/reward} with Nuh, who called his people a thousand years less fifty, night and day, and {trap}only a few believed.{/trap} So do not grieve for those who refuse. {idea}Allah guides whom He wills.{/idea}
now: You have been gently reminding your brother to pray for three years. He still rolls his eyes. {trap}You feel like a failure.{/trap} Nuh kept going for centuries. {idea}Your job is the calling, with kindness. The heart is in Allah's hand.{/idea}
old: If they have not changed by now, I have failed.
new: I am asked to be faithful and patient. Guidance belongs to Allah.
try: Make dua tonight, by name, for one person you have been trying to help, and let go of the timeline.

title: The ship that saved them became a sign.
subtitle: Every boat on the water is a reminder
then: Allah saved Nuh and those who believed with him on the ship. Ibn Kathir mentions the view of Qatadah that the ship remained on Mount Judi, or that {idea}sailing itself was left as a reminder{/idea} of how {reward}Allah saved mankind from the Flood.{/reward}
now: You ride the ferry to work, or watch a cargo ship crawl along the horizon on holiday. {idea}It floats because Allah lets it.{/idea} The verse turns an ordinary commute into a memory of rescue.
old: A boat is just a machine that works.
new: Every ship on the water is a quiet sign of Allah saving the believers.
try: Next time you see water, a river, sea or even rain on a window, say alhamdulillah for being kept safe.

title: Worship Him and fear Him. That is best for you.
subtitle: Ibrahim's opening words to his people

row.title: good
sub: here and in the next life

then: Allah tells the story of Ibrahim to people in Makkah facing the same kind of idol worship. Ibrahim called his people to {idea}worship and fear Allah alone.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains that doing so brings {reward}good in this world and the next{/reward} and keeps harm away in both.
now: You think of faith as a list of things you cannot do, while your friends seem freer. Ibrahim framed it the other way. {reward}This is better for you, if you only knew.{/reward} {idea}The command is a gift wrapped as a duty.{/idea}
old: Religion mainly takes things away from me.
new: Worshipping Allah and being mindful of Him is the best thing I can do for myself.
try: Pick one command you find heavy and write down one way it actually protects you.

title: Seek your provision from the One who has it.
subtitle: Idols cannot feed you
then: Ibrahim told his people their idols were {trap}made-up names for created things{/trap} that could not provide. Ibn Kathir says the phrase emphasizes {idea}asking Allah alone,{/idea} as in You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Eat from His provision, worship Him, {reward}and thank Him.{/reward}
now: The rent is due and you refresh the banking app three times. You start treating your manager's mood like the source of your survival. {trap}That quietly becomes an idol.{/trap} {idea}The salary is a means. The Provider is Allah.{/idea}
old: My income depends on the people who pay me.
new: People are doors. Provision comes from Allah, so I ask Him first.
try: Before checking your bank balance next time, make a short dua for provision.

title: The messenger's job is to convey clearly.
subtitle: Responsibility ends at a clear message
then: Ibrahim warned that {trap}nations before had denied{/trap} and saw the result. Qatadah called this {reward}consolation for the Prophet ﷺ.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes the Messengers only {idea}convey the message as commanded.{/idea} Allah guides whom He wills.
now: Your friend asked about Islam, you explained it as well as you could, and he shrugged. You keep replaying the conversation, sure you ruined it. {idea}You were asked to be clear and kind.{/idea} {reward}The result is not on your shoulders.{/reward}
old: If they do not accept, I did it wrong.
new: My part is to say it clearly and well. Hearts are turned by Allah.
try: Let go of one conversation you keep replaying, and make dua for that person instead.

title: The One who began you can do it again.
subtitle: Your own beginning is proof of the return
then: Ibrahim's people denied life after death. Ibn Kathir says he pointed them to {idea}their own souls:{/idea} Allah made them when they were nothing, then they could hear and see. {reward}The One who started this can repeat it,{/reward} and it is easy for Him.
now: You hold a newborn niece in the maternity ward, and nine months ago she did not exist. {idea}That is the argument.{/idea} If a person can come from nothing, coming back is not the strange part.
old: Being brought back after death is hard to believe.
new: I came from nothing once. Bringing me back is easy for the One who did that.
try: Look at a baby photo of yourself today and remember Allah made you from nothing.

title: Travel and look at how creation began.
subtitle: The world as a book to read
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Ibrahim taught them to {idea}contemplate the visible signs:{/idea} stars, plains, mountains, valleys, rivers, fruits, oceans. All of it shows {reward}a Creator who says Be and it is,{/reward} and who will bring forth the final creation.
now: On a road trip you pass a mountain range at sunset and everyone grabs their phones. {idea}The verse asks for a second look,{/idea} past the picture. Who started all this, and what does it say about what comes next?
old: Nature is just the backdrop of my life.
new: Every mountain and river is a sign that Allah creates, and will create again.
try: Go outside today and look at one natural thing for a full minute without your phone.

title: Mercy and punishment are His to give.
subtitle: And every one of us goes back to Him
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is {idea}the Ruler in control{/idea} whose judgement no one can overturn. No one questions Him; it is people who will be questioned. Whatever He decides is fair, for He {reward}cannot be unjust in the slightest.{/reward} To Him everyone returns.
now: You hear of someone's hard life and someone else's easy one, and a small voice says this is not fair. {idea}You only see a slice.{/idea} The verse invites trust, and a turn to your own return, rather than a verdict on His.
old: I can judge whether Allah's decisions are fair.
new: Allah is perfectly just, and my job is to prepare for my own return to Him.
try: Ask Allah today for His mercy, in your own words, for yourself and someone you love.

title: No escape on earth or in the sky.
subtitle: And no protector besides Allah
then: Ibrahim told his people that {trap}no one in heaven or earth can flee from Allah.{/trap} Ibn Kathir describes Him as the Subduer above His servants. Everything is {idea}in need of Him,{/idea} while He needs nothing. Besides Him there is {reward}no protector or helper.{/reward}
now: You avoid the prayer mat after a bad week, like hiding from a teacher after skipping homework. {trap}You cannot get out of His sight.{/trap} {reward}You also do not need to.{/reward} The One you are hiding from is the only real shelter.
old: When I mess up, I should keep my distance from Allah.
new: I cannot escape Allah, so the safest place to go is back to Him.
try: If you have been avoiding prayer, pray just the next one, even if it feels awkward.

title: Denying the meeting cuts off hope.
subtitle: What rejecting Allah's signs leads to
then: Ibn Kathir says those who disbelieved in Allah's signs and {trap}denied the Resurrection{/trap} will have no share in His mercy. This closes Ibrahim's argument about life after death. {idea}Hope and belief in the meeting go together.{/idea}
now: You hear yourself say, "God is merciful, it will be fine," while you ignore Him for months. {trap}Hope that never turns toward Him{/trap} is just a nice thought. {idea}Real hope moves your feet{/idea} toward the meeting.
old: Allah's mercy covers me whatever I believe or do.
new: Hope in Allah's mercy grows from believing in Him and in meeting Him.
try: Turn one vague hope today into one small act, a prayer, a charity, an apology.

title: Out of arguments, they reached for fire.
subtitle: And Allah made the fire safe
then: Ibn Kathir says the proof was clear against them, so {trap}they turned to power and strength.{/trap} They built a huge fire and threw Ibrahim in with a catapult. {reward}Allah made it cool and safe,{/reward} and he came out unharmed. {idea}In that are signs for those who believe.{/idea}
now: You lose an argument with your sibling, so you raise your voice, bring up old mistakes, slam the door. {trap}That is the fire move, in small.{/trap} The verse makes you notice when you swap reasons for force.
old: When I cannot win with words, pressure is fair.
new: Reaching for force means I have run out of truth. Allah protects those who stand with it.
try: In your next disagreement, if you notice your voice rising, stop and say one calm sentence instead.

title: Bonds built on falsehood turn into blame.
subtitle: Friendships held together by idols
then: Ibrahim told his people they gathered around idols {trap}to keep friendship and love among themselves.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says on the Day this turns to hatred: followers and leaders curse each other. He cites the verse that friends become foes {reward}except those who have taqwa.{/reward}
now: Your friend group bonds over gossip, or over the same bad habit every weekend. It feels like closeness. {trap}It is a bond that will not hold.{/trap} {reward}The friends who remind you of Allah are the ones still standing with you later.{/reward}
old: Going along with the group keeps my friendships safe.
new: Only friendships built on good will survive the Day. The rest turn into blame.
try: Think of what really holds one of your friendships together, and add one good thing to it this week.

title: One believer, then a journey to his Lord.
subtitle: Lut believes, and they leave together
then: Of all his people, {reward}only Lut believed in Ibrahim,{/reward} along with Sarah. Ibn Kathir says they left {idea}so they could follow their religion openly.{/idea} Qatadah said they went from Kutha near Kufa to Syria. This surah came as Makkah's Muslims were themselves about to emigrate.
now: You move out of a flatshare where you could not pray in peace, or change jobs to escape a place that wore your faith down. People call it running away. {idea}Sometimes leaving is moving toward Allah.{/idea} {reward}One friend who believes with you is enough to start.{/reward}
old: If I leave a hard place, I have failed.
new: Leaving for the sake of my faith can be a journey to my Lord, not a defeat.
try: Thank the one person in your life who most supports your faith, today.

title: He gave up his home and gained a lineage of prophets.
subtitle: What Ibrahim received after leaving

row.title: prophethood
sub: and the Book in his line

then: After Ibrahim left his people, Allah gave him Ishaq and then Ya'qub. Ibn Kathir notes that {reward}every Prophet after him came from his descendants,{/reward} down to Muhammad ﷺ through Isma'il. He was also given {idea}reward in this world{/idea} and is among the righteous in the next.
now: You turned down a well paid offer because it would have meant compromising your deen. Months later you still wonder if that was foolish. {reward}Ibrahim's story says what you give up for Allah is not lost.{/reward} It comes back in forms you did not plan.
old: What I give up for Allah is simply gone.
new: What I leave for Allah, He replaces with more, in this life and the next.
try: Remember one thing you gave up for Allah and say alhamdulillah for whatever came after it.

title: Lut named what no one else would.
subtitle: Speaking up when wrong has become normal
then: Lut, who had emigrated with Ibrahim, was sent to the people of Sadum. Ibn Kathir says he {idea}denounced their immoral deeds,{/idea} a sin that {trap}no one before them had committed.{/trap} They also rejected Allah and opposed His Messenger.
now: At your workplace, padding expenses is just what everyone does. Nobody blinks. {trap}When a wrong becomes normal, it gets harder to see.{/trap} {idea}Lut's courage was to call it what it was, starting with his own people's conduct.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me does it, it cannot be that bad.
new: Wrong stays wrong even when it is normal. I can be the one who quietly does not join in.
try: Notice one thing everyone around you does that you know is wrong, and step out of it today.

title: Wrong done openly, with no one objecting.
subtitle: Gatherings where evil is shared and cheered
then: Ibn Kathir says they also {trap}robbed and killed travellers on the road.{/trap} In their gatherings they did and said shameful things and {idea}did not stop one another.{/idea} Asked to change, they mocked: bring Allah's punishment if you are truthful.
now: The group chat turns cruel about someone not in it. Everyone sends a laughing emoji. {trap}No one says stop.{/trap} {idea}The verse puts the spotlight on the gathering,{/idea} and on whether you are one of the people who just goes along.
old: I did not say anything bad, I was only there.
new: A gathering where wrong goes unchallenged shares in it. I can be the one who objects.
try: Next time a conversation turns cruel or shameful, change the subject or leave it.

title: When mocked, Lut turned to his Lord.
subtitle: A prophet's short prayer for help

key.label: What to do when no one listens

then: Ibn Kathir says their reply showed {trap}disbelief, scorn and stubbornness.{/trap} So the Prophet Lut {idea}asked Allah for help:{/idea} My Lord, support me against the corrupting people. After long calling, he handed the matter to Allah.
now: You tried to stop something wrong at work and got laughed at in the meeting. On the drive home you rehearse comebacks. {idea}Lut did not rehearse comebacks.{/idea} He took it to his Lord in one sentence.
old: If people mock me for doing right, I have to win it back myself.
new: When I am mocked for the truth, I can hand it to Allah and ask for His help.
try: Turn one frustration from today into a one-line dua: my Lord, help me with this.

title: The same visitors brought joy and warning.
subtitle: Angels come to Ibrahim on their way to Lut
then: Ibn Kathir says when Lut asked for help, {idea}Allah sent angels to help him.{/idea} They came first to Ibrahim as guests and he hosted them. They gave him {reward}news of a righteous son from Sarah,{/reward} then told him they were sent to destroy the town of Lut, {trap}whose people were wrongdoers.{/trap}
now: You made a dua last month and heard nothing back. Meanwhile, quietly, the right person was already on the way, the job offer already being drafted. {idea}Lut's answer was walking toward him{/idea} before he knew it.
old: If nothing has changed, my dua was not heard.
new: Allah's answer may already be on its way, arriving by a route I cannot see.
try: Repeat one dua you made recently, this time with full trust that it is being answered.

title: Ibrahim spoke up for a town, and was told: We know.
subtitle: Mercy for others, and who is saved
then: Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim {reward}began to speak up for them,{/reward} hoping to win them more time to be guided. The angels replied that they knew who was there. Lut and his family would be saved, {trap}except his wife,{/trap} because she supported her people in their wrongdoing.
now: Your cousin is in trouble and your first instinct is to plead for him, to buy him time. {reward}That mercy is Ibrahim's mercy.{/reward} {idea}The verse also reminds you that no family name saves you.{/idea} Your own choices do.
old: Being from a good family will see me through.
new: I can plead for others with mercy, but my own stand is what counts for me.
try: Make a sincere dua today for someone you know who has gone astray.

title: He was worried for his guests. They said: do not fear.
subtitle: Lut's distress and the angels' comfort
then: The angels came to Lut looking like handsome young men. Ibn Kathir says he {trap}was distressed{/trap}: if he hosted them he feared what his people would do, and if he did not, he still feared for them. He did not know who they were. They told him {reward}not to fear or grieve.{/reward}
now: You are lying awake about something you feel you alone must fix, a sick parent, a debt, a child who is struggling. {trap}It all feels on your shoulders.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the thing you are anxious about is the very door Allah's help comes through.{/idea}
old: Everything depends on me handling this.
new: I do my best, and Allah's help may already be standing in front of me.
try: Tonight before sleep, hand one worry to Allah in a dua and try not to pick it back up.

title: Because they kept rebelling.
subtitle: Why the punishment came
then: The angels said the punishment would come {trap}because they had been defiantly disobedient.{/trap} Ibn Kathir describes the town being overturned and stones sent upon it. {idea}It came after long warning and open mockery,{/idea} not without cause.
now: You have been told many times about one habit, by your conscience, by a friend, by a verse you keep meeting. {trap}You keep saying later.{/trap} {idea}The verse is a sober reminder that persisting is itself a choice.{/idea} {reward}Turning back is still open.{/reward}
old: Warnings can be put off forever.
new: Persisting after being warned is a choice I make, and so is turning back today.
try: Pick the warning you have ignored the longest and take one small step on it today.

title: A ruin left as a sign for those who think.
subtitle: Passing by and actually reflecting
then: Ibn Kathir says the place became a lake that remains {idea}a lesson to mankind{/idea} until the Day of Resurrection. He links it to the verse addressed to those who {trap}pass by them morning and night: will you not reflect?{/trap}
now: You scroll past news of a ruined life, a scandal, a collapse, and keep scrolling. {idea}The verse asks you to use your reason{/idea} and turn the question toward yourself. What in my own life would I want to change before it is too late?
old: Other people's downfall is just news.
new: Every ruin I see is a sign, if I stop and think about my own path.
try: The next time a story of someone's downfall reaches you, pause and ask what lesson it holds for you.

title: Worship, keep the Last Day in view, harm no one.
subtitle: Shu'ayb's three-part call to Madyan

row.title: one life
sub: the scales are part of faith

then: Shu'ayb, their brother, called Madyan to {idea}worship Allah alone and look to the Last Day.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says spreading corruption meant {trap}going around doing evil to people:{/trap} they cheated in weights and measures and ambushed people on the road.
now: You round up your hours on the timesheet. You describe a used car as better than it is. {trap}Small cheats in ordinary trade.{/trap} Shu'ayb's call puts the Last Day right next to the scales. {idea}Faith shows up in how you deal.{/idea}
old: My religion is about prayer, not about how I do business.
new: Worshipping Allah and remembering the Last Day show in honest weights and fair deals.
try: Check one transaction or timesheet this week and make it exactly honest.

title: They denied him, and the ground shook.
subtitle: The end of Madyan
then: Madyan rejected Shu'ayb. Ibn Kathir says Allah destroyed them with {trap}a mighty earthquake{/trap} and a shout, and their story is told in detail in other surahs. {idea}They were taken in the very homes{/idea} they trusted.
now: You feel safe in your house, your routine, your locked front door. {trap}Safety can feel like it comes from walls.{/trap} {idea}The verse quietly points to the true source of safety,{/idea} and asks whether you are listening to the reminders around you.
old: As long as my home is secure, I am safe.
new: Real safety comes from listening to Allah's guidance, not from my walls.
try: Say the dua for leaving your home today, and mean it as handing your safety to Allah.

title: Clever people, made to love their own mistakes.
subtitle: 'Ad and Thamud, whose ruins the Arabs knew
then: Ibn Kathir says 'Ad lived in the sand hills near Hadramawt and Thamud in Al-Hijr. {idea}The Arabs knew those places and often passed them.{/idea} The verse says {trap}Shaytan made their deeds seem good{/trap} and turned them away, though they were people of understanding.
now: You are sharp, educated, good with arguments. You build a perfect case for why your shortcut is fine. {trap}Intelligence can polish a mistake until it shines.{/trap} {idea}The verse warns that seeing clearly needs more than brains.{/idea}
old: I am too smart to be fooled.
new: A clever mind can still be led astray when wrong is made to look right.
try: Take one thing you have convinced yourself is fine, and ask someone wise and honest what they think.

title: Wealth, power and position could not outrun Him.
subtitle: Qarun, Fir'awn and Haman
then: Ibn Kathir describes Qarun as {trap}owner of great wealth and immense treasures,{/trap} Fir'awn as king of Egypt and Haman as his minister. Musa came to them with {idea}clear signs,{/idea} but they were arrogant in the land, and {trap}they could not outrun Allah.{/trap}
now: You get the promotion, the corner office, a little power over others' schedules. It is easy to start talking down. {trap}Arrogance grows quietly with every win.{/trap} {idea}The verse reminds you that no position puts you out of Allah's reach.{/idea}
old: With enough money or rank, I am untouchable.
new: Wealth and power do not put me beyond Allah. They test whether I stay humble.
try: Do one humble act today for someone who has less power than you at work or home.

title: Allah did not wrong them. They wronged themselves.
subtitle: Each was taken for their own sin
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}their punishments fit their crimes.{/idea} 'Ad, who asked who is stronger than us, met a violent wind. Thamud were struck by the blast, Qarun swallowed by the earth, Fir'awn and Haman drowned. {trap}It happened for what they did with their own hands.{/trap}
now: Your health slips after years of ignoring the doctor. A friendship breaks after the third betrayal. {trap}It is tempting to blame life or fate.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the honest sentence is: I did this to myself.{/idea} {reward}That sentence is also where repair starts.{/reward}
old: When things go wrong for me, it is unfair.
new: Allah never wrongs anyone. Much of my harm comes from my own hands, and so can my repair.
try: Name one problem you have been blaming on others, and take one step to own your part today.

title: Leaning on anything but Allah is a spider's house.
subtitle: The weakest of homes
then: This verse gives the surah its name. Ibn Kathir says people who turned to other gods for help and provision were like {trap}someone holding on to a spider's web.{/trap} The believer has {reward}grasped the most trustworthy handle,{/reward} which never breaks.
now: You lean on the follower count, the savings pot, the connection who "knows people". {trap}It looks like a structure. It is a web.{/trap} {idea}When the wind comes, only what is tied to Allah holds.{/idea}
old: My plans and connections are what keep me standing.
new: Anything I lean on instead of Allah is as thin as a spider's web.
try: Next time you see a spider's web, name one thing you are leaning on too hard.

title: He knows exactly what you call on besides Him.
subtitle: Nothing you lean on is hidden

row.title: private
sub: nobody knows I depend on it

then: After the spider parable, Ibn Kathir says Allah {trap}warns those who associate others with Him{/trap} that {idea}He knows what they do{/idea} and the rivals they set up. He is the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.
now: No one knows you check your horoscope app before big decisions, or that you secretly trust a lucky charm. {idea}Allah knows.{/idea} {reward}That is not only a warning. It means He also knows the moment you let go and turn to Him.{/reward}
old: What I quietly rely on is my own private business.
new: Allah knows every hidden thing I lean on, and every time I turn back to Him.
try: Let go of one small superstition or private crutch today and say tawakkaltu ala Allah.

title: The examples are for everyone, the understanding for few.
subtitle: Parables that need a thinking heart
then: Ibn Kathir says no one understands these examples {idea}except those with deep knowledge.{/idea} He reports that 'Amr bin Murrah said that whenever he met a verse of the Book he did not understand, {trap}it grieved him,{/trap} because of this verse.
now: You have heard the spider parable a dozen times in khutbahs and nodded along. {trap}Hearing is not the same as understanding.{/trap} {idea}The verse invites you to sit with one example until it changes something in you.{/idea}
old: I know that story already.
new: Allah's examples open up only to those who keep thinking about them.
try: Choose one parable from this surah and spend five minutes today thinking about what it means for you.

title: The heavens and earth were made with purpose.
subtitle: Creation is not a game
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah created the heavens and earth {idea}with truth, for a higher purpose{/idea} than mere play, so that {reward}every person is rewarded for what he strives for.{/reward} It is clear evidence that Allah alone creates and controls.
now: Some days at work feel like pointless loops, emails, meetings, more emails. {trap}You start to wonder if any of it means anything.{/trap} {idea}The verse says the whole universe was made with purpose,{/idea} so your effort in it counts.
old: Life is random and my effort does not really matter.
new: The world was created with truth, so what I strive for is seen and rewarded.
try: Look at the sky tonight and say one thing you are striving for that you hope Allah rewards.

title: Prayer pulls you away from wrong. Remembering Allah is greater.
subtitle: Recite, pray, and let it change you
then: Ibn Kathir cites a man telling the Prophet ﷺ that someone prayed at night but stole by morning. He replied, {reward}what you are saying will stop him.{/reward} Prayer helps a person give up evil, but {idea}remembering Allah is the higher goal.{/idea} Abu Al-'Aliyah named three marks: sincerity, fear of Allah, and remembrance.
now: You pray five times, and still snap at your spouse or lie at work. {trap}A voice says you are a fraud, so why bother.{/trap} {idea}Keep praying.{/idea} Slowly, prayer done with sincerity and remembrance starts pulling you back from the things you hate in yourself.
old: If I still sin, my prayer is worthless.
new: Prayer is what slowly pulls me away from wrong, so I keep it, especially when I am struggling.
try: In your next prayer, slow down for one verse and actually think of Allah while you say it.

title: Argue only in the way that is best.
subtitle: How to talk faith with those who have a scripture
then: Ibn Kathir links this to the command to Musa and Harun to speak mildly even to Fir'awn. Debate with those who have a scripture was to be {idea}in the way that is best{/idea}, because that works. On reports from their books, the Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}do not believe them and do not deny them{/reward}, but say we believe in what was sent to us and to you.
now: A coworker who goes to church asks you about Ramadan at the coffee machine. Or a comment thread online turns into a fight about God. {trap}The urge is to win.{/trap} The verse asks for something harder: {idea}start with what you share, and speak so they want to keep listening.{/idea}
old: If I really believe I am right, I should crush the other side.
new: Being right is not enough. The way I say it is part of the truth I carry.
try: Next time faith comes up with someone of another religion, begin with one thing you both believe.

title: The same Sender, the same kind of Book.
subtitle: Who recognized the Quran when it came
then: Ibn Kathir explains: just as Allah sent Books to earlier messengers, He sent this one to Muhammad ﷺ. {reward}Scholars of earlier scripture{/reward}, such as Abdullah bin Salam and Salman Al-Farisi, recognized it. So did some of Quraysh. Only those who {trap}cover the truth{/trap} rejected it, like someone covering an eye to block the sun.
now: You read something that rings true, and you know it. Then you scroll past, because accepting it would mean changing a habit. {trap}You tell yourself you need more proof.{/trap} Sometimes the problem is not the evidence. {idea}It is the hand over the eye.{/idea}
old: I will believe when I am fully convinced.
new: Often I am already convinced. What I lack is the will to act on it.
try: Name one truth you already know but keep postponing. Take one small step toward it today.

title: He never read a book, so no one could say he copied.
subtitle: The unlettered Prophet as proof

row.title: it came to him
sub: everyone knew he could not read

then: Ibn Kathir notes that the Prophet ﷺ lived among his people for years and {idea}never read or wrote anything{/idea}. Everyone knew it. He had scribes to write the revelation for him. If he had been literate, falsifiers would say he copied old books. {trap}They said it anyway{/trap}, calling it tales of the ancients.
now: Someone you know changes for the better, quietly and fast. A cousin who was lost now prays and is kind. People in the family chat say, {trap}it is just a phase, someone got into his head.{/trap} The verse shows how {idea}people who do not want a truth will invent a source for it.{/idea}
old: There must be an ordinary explanation for anything remarkable.
new: Sometimes the ordinary explanation is the one that has been ruled out.
try: Read a short passage of the Quran today and remember it came through a man who could not read.

title: This Book lives in hearts, not just on pages.
subtitle: The Quran preserved in the chests of people

key.label: A book that cannot be erased

then: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith in Sahih Muslim: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ He is revealing {idea}a Book that water cannot wash away{/idea}, recited asleep and awake. It is kept in the hearts of those given knowledge. Those who deny it are {trap}wrongdoers who know the truth and turn away.{/trap}
now: Your phone dies on the bus. No app, no screen. What is left is what you carry inside: a few surahs from childhood, maybe the one your grandmother taught you. {reward}That part no battery can take.{/reward} {idea}The Book was always meant to live there.{/idea}
old: The Quran is on my phone whenever I need it.
new: What I truly own of the Quran is what lives in my heart.
try: Memorize one short verse today, even three words at a time.

title: Show us a miracle, they said.
subtitle: The demand for signs and the honest reply
then: The idolaters kept asking for a miracle, like the she-camel given to Salih. Ibn Kathir says Allah knew {trap}they were only being stubborn{/trap}, testing the Prophet ﷺ. The reply: signs are in Allah's hands, and {idea}my job is to warn clearly.{/idea}
now: You tell God, if You are there, fix this one thing by Friday and I will pray. Or a friend says, I will believe when I see a miracle. {trap}We set the terms and wait.{/trap} {idea}The messenger never accepted that deal. He just kept delivering the message.{/idea}
old: If God gave me one clear sign, I would change.
new: Signs are not mine to order. My part is to respond to what has already come.
try: Drop one deal you have been making with Allah. Do the good thing without the condition.

title: Is the Book itself not sign enough?
subtitle: The miracle that was already in their ears

row.title: something new
sub: a sign we have not seen

then: Ibn Kathir calls the Quran {idea}greater than all other miracles{/idea}. The most eloquent Arabs could not produce even one surah like it. It was recited to them, telling of past nations and settling disputes, from a man who could not read. Yet they {trap}kept asking for something else.{/trap}
now: You wait for a sign: a dream, a stranger saying the right thing, a sudden feeling. Meanwhile the mushaf sits on the shelf, or the app is three taps away. {idea}The sign is already in your hand.{/idea} {reward}Mercy and reminder{/reward}, open whenever you are.
old: I am waiting for something to move me.
new: The thing that can move me is already here, waiting to be read.
try: Before looking for answers elsewhere today, read one page of the Quran slowly.

title: Allah is witness between us. That is enough.
subtitle: When you cannot convince, leave it with the Witness
then: After all the arguments, the Prophet ﷺ is told to say: {idea}Allah is enough as witness{/idea} between me and you. Ibn Kathir explains that Allah knows what each side says. If the Prophet ﷺ were lying about Him, He would have seized him. Those who {trap}trusted falsehood{/trap} are the real losers.
now: You have explained yourself in the group chat five times. Nobody believes you about what happened at work. You lie awake writing the sixth message. {idea}Allah saw it all.{/idea} {reward}You do not need everyone's verdict when you have His.{/reward}
old: I need people to understand my side or I cannot rest.
new: Allah already knows my side. His knowledge is enough.
try: Leave one argument unsent today. Say quietly, Allah is enough as my witness.

title: They dared the punishment to come quickly.
subtitle: A delay is not a cancellation
then: The idolaters mocked the warning by asking for punishment to come right away. Ibn Kathir compares it to their saying, if this is the truth, rain stones on us. Were it not for {idea}a term Allah had set{/idea}, it would have come. {trap}It will still come, suddenly.{/trap}
now: You keep doing the thing you know is wrong, and nothing bad happens. A week, a year. {trap}The quiet starts to feel like permission.{/trap} {idea}The verse reframes the silence: it is time on loan{/idea}, a door still open to turn back.
old: If it were really wrong, something would have happened by now.
new: The delay is mercy and a deadline at once. It is my chance to turn.
try: Pick one habit you have been getting away with. Stop it today while the door is open.

title: They ask for it, while it already surrounds them.
subtitle: The danger is closer than the dare
then: The verse repeats their demand, almost in disbelief. They kept urging the Prophet ﷺ to hasten punishment. Ibn Kathir says {trap}it will undoubtedly befall them{/trap}. The point is irony: {idea}they ask for something that already encircles them.{/idea}
now: A man laughs off his doctor's warning about smoking: if it was going to get me, it would have. The damage is already inside, quietly growing. {trap}Mocking a warning does not move you away from it.{/trap} {idea}Only changing direction does.{/idea}
old: Warnings are for later. I am fine right now.
new: Where I am heading is already shaping where I stand.
try: Take one warning you have brushed off, from a doctor, a parent, or your own heart, and act on it.

title: Taste what you used to do.
subtitle: Deeds come back to the one who did them
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the punishment covers them on every side, and then come the words, {trap}taste what you used to do{/trap}. He calls the words a rebuke on top of the pain. {idea}Nothing in it is random. It is their own deeds coming back.{/idea}
now: Every day you make small choices: the snapped reply to your mother, the honest word at work, the prayer you got up for. {idea}Each one is something you will meet again.{/idea} {reward}That works for good deeds too.{/reward} What would you like waiting for you?
old: What happens to me in the end is out of my hands.
new: What I meet in the end is shaped by what I do today.
try: Do one good deed today on purpose, thinking: this is something I want to meet again.

title: My earth is wide, so worship Me.
subtitle: When one place closes, the earth is still open

key.label: What is fixed, what can move

then: This surah came in a time of harsh persecution in Makkah. Ibn Kathir explains: when believers could not practice their faith, {idea}Allah's earth was spacious{/idea}. Many moved to Abyssinia, where the Negus {reward}gave them refuge and honored them{/reward}. Later the Prophet ﷺ and the rest went to Madinah.
now: The job where you cannot pray on time and feel pressure every day. The friend group where staying means slowly losing yourself. {trap}You feel stuck, as if this is the only option.{/trap} {idea}Allah's earth is wide.{/idea} There are other jobs, other circles, other cities.
old: I have no choice but to stay where I am.
new: Places are many. What I must protect is my worship, wherever that takes me.
try: Name one place or circle that keeps pulling you from Allah. Write down one real alternative.

title: Every soul tastes death, then returns to Us.
subtitle: Why fear of moving should not stop you
then: Right after the call to migrate, this reminder. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}wherever you are, death will catch up with you{/idea}, so be where Allah commands. The fear of the road was real for the emigrants. But {reward}the obedient will have the best reward{/reward} when they return to Him.
now: You do not take the better path because of what might go wrong: the new city, the hard conversation, the career change for the sake of your deen. {trap}You stay put to stay safe.{/trap} {idea}But nowhere is safe from death.{/idea} The only real question is where you want it to find you.
old: Staying where I am keeps me safe.
new: No place keeps me from death. So I choose the place that pleases Allah.
try: Think of one hard right step you keep avoiding out of fear. Make one small move toward it.

title: Those who left homes behind get lofty homes forever.
subtitle: The reward waiting for those who believe and act
then: The believers in Makkah were being told to leave homes behind for their faith. This verse tells them what is waiting. Ibn Kathir describes {reward}lofty dwellings with rivers beneath{/reward}, which they live in forever. It is called {idea}the reward of the workers{/idea}: earned by belief and deeds.
now: You turned down the job with the bad environment. You moved out of the flat share where you could not pray in peace. {trap}It felt like losing a home.{/trap} {reward}The verse says a better home is being built{/reward}, one you will never have to leave.
old: When I give something up for Allah, I just lose it.
new: What I give up for Allah is exchanged for something lasting.
try: Remember one thing you gave up for Allah. Thank Him for the chance, and ask Him to accept it.

title: They were patient, and they relied on their Lord.
subtitle: The two traits of those who get the reward
then: Ibn Kathir says these are people {idea}patient in holding to their religion{/idea}, who migrated and left family behind to seek Allah's Face. And they {reward}put their trust in their Lord{/reward} in all their affairs, of faith and of daily life alike.
now: Month three of looking for work. The rent reminder on your phone. Your parents asking every Sunday if anything came through. {trap}You try to carry it all on your own back.{/trap} {idea}Patience is staying steady. Trust is handing the outcome to Allah.{/idea} You need both.
old: If I just push hard enough, I can get through this alone.
new: I keep going, and I leave the result with my Lord.
try: Name the worry weighing on you most. Do your part today, then say: I rely on Allah for the rest.

title: The bird carries no lunchbox, yet it is fed.
subtitle: Provision is not tied to one place
then: The emigrants feared leaving Makkah meant losing their living. Ibn Kathir says {idea}provision is not limited to one place{/idea}. Many creatures cannot gather or store food, yet Allah feeds them, from ants underground to fish in the sea. {reward}The emigrants' provision became greater than before.{/reward}
now: The thought that keeps you in the wrong job: where else would I earn this? The bank app, the bills, the kids' school fees. {trap}You treat one salary as the source of life.{/trap} Look at the pigeons on the window ledge. {idea}They have no savings, and they are fed.{/idea}
old: My income depends entirely on where I am now.
new: My provision comes from Allah, and He can send it anywhere.
try: Watch a bird for one minute today. Then say, Allah provides for it and for me.

title: They knew Allah created everything, yet looked elsewhere.
subtitle: Admitting the Creator but trusting others
then: The idolaters of Makkah admitted Allah alone created the heavens, the earth, the sun and the moon. Ibn Kathir notes their own pilgrimage chant said He had no partner, then added one. His point: {idea}if He alone creates and controls, why worship or trust anyone else?{/idea} {trap}That gap is the delusion.{/trap}
now: Ask yourself who controls your life and you will say Allah. Then watch where your heart goes when the contract is late: {trap}the boss, the connection, the lucky charm, the horoscope app.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks you to close the gap between what you say and where you lean.{/idea}
old: Of course I believe Allah is in control.
new: If I really believe it, my worry and my hope should go to Him first.
try: Next time you feel anxious today, notice who you think of first. Turn to Allah before them.

title: More for some, less for others, by His knowledge.
subtitle: Why provision differs between people
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah made people and their provision different, {idea}some rich and some poor{/idea}, and He knows best what suits each of them. He alone decides this, so {trap}there is no reason to turn to anyone else{/trap} for what only He gives.
now: Your friend posts the new car. Your cousin's wedding costs more than your year's salary. You check your own account and feel small. {trap}The comparison starts to feel like a judgement.{/trap} {idea}The amount is a measure Allah fitted to you{/idea}, not a grade on your worth.
old: If I have less, I must be worth less, or forgotten.
new: My share was measured by One who knows me. It is not a verdict on my worth.
try: Mute one account that makes you envious today. Thank Allah for three things you already have.

title: Rain brings dead earth back. Who sends it?
subtitle: Praise the One they already named
then: Asked who sends rain and revives the earth, the idolaters again answered {idea}Allah{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ is told to respond: {reward}praise be to Allah{/reward}. Ibn Kathir explains that since dominion is His alone, worship should be His alone. Most of them {trap}did not reason it through.{/trap}
now: A storm breaks after a heatwave and everyone on your street steps outside. The air smells of wet soil. The weather app called it a front moving in. {idea}It is also a sign that the One who revives dead earth can revive a dead heart.{/idea}
old: Rain is just weather.
new: Rain is a reminder of Who brings life back, to land and to me.
try: Next time it rains, step out for a moment and say, Alhamdulillah.

title: This life is play. The next one is real life.
subtitle: What lasts against what passes
then: Ibn Kathir explains how {trap}small and short this world is{/trap}, soon to end, nothing more than play. The Hereafter is {reward}the true everlasting life{/reward}. If people really knew, he says, they would prefer what lasts over what passes away.
now: You lose an evening to a game, or a show, or an argument in the comments. It felt huge in the moment. Next morning you cannot remember why. {idea}That is the verse in miniature.{/idea} Much of what grips you now will look like that from the Hereafter.
old: What happens now is what really matters.
new: Now is the game. What comes after is the life.
try: Pick one hour today you would usually spend on play and give ten minutes of it to something lasting.

title: Sincere on the stormy sea, forgetful on dry land.
subtitle: Calling on Allah only in danger
then: Ibn Kathir tells of 'Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl fleeing by sea after the conquest of Makkah. The ship rocked and the crew said, pray to your Lord alone. He realized: {idea}if only He saves at sea, only He saves on land.{/idea} He vowed to go to the Prophet ﷺ, and {reward}he did.{/reward}
now: The turbulence on the flight. The night in the hospital corridor waiting for news. You prayed like never before. {trap}Then the plane landed, the test came back fine, and life went back to normal.{/trap} {idea}The One who answered then is the same One today.{/idea}
old: I pray hardest when I am in trouble. That is natural.
new: The One who saved me in the storm is holding me on calm ground too.
try: Recall one time Allah got you through something. Thank Him for it today, on an ordinary day.

title: Saved, then ungrateful. They will come to know.
subtitle: Enjoying the rescue while denying the Rescuer
then: This completes the picture of the ship. Once safe, they {trap}denied what Allah gave them{/trap} and went back to enjoying life as if nothing happened. The verse ends with a quiet warning: {idea}they are going to know.{/idea}
now: You recovered from the illness. The debt got paid off. The family member came home safe. {trap}A month later you are complaining as if none of it happened.{/trap} {idea}Gratitude is the proof that you understood who saved you.{/idea}
old: That was a hard time, but it is over now.
new: It is over because of Allah. Remembering that is my thanks.
try: Write down one rescue in your life. Put it somewhere you will see it next week.

title: Safe in the sanctuary while others were snatched away.
subtitle: A blessing so constant they stopped seeing it

key.label: What they did with the gift

then: Ibn Kathir reminds that Allah made the sanctuary of Makkah {reward}a place where anyone who entered was safe{/reward}, while desert tribes around raided and killed one another. He links it to Surah Quraysh: fed against hunger, safe from fear. Yet Quraysh {trap}answered that blessing with idols{/trap} and rejected the Prophet ﷺ.
now: Your home has a lock that works. Your street is quiet at night. You open the news and see people elsewhere losing everything. {idea}Safety is a blessing you can stop noticing.{/idea} {trap}Then it becomes a background you take for granted.{/trap}
old: Being safe is just normal.
new: My safety is a favor from Allah, and it asks for thanks.
try: Tonight when you lock your door, thank Allah by name for keeping your home safe.

title: No one is more wrong than a liar about Allah.
subtitle: Inventing words for Allah, or denying His truth
then: Ibn Kathir explains two people who do the most wrong. One {trap}claims Allah revealed something to him{/trap} when He did not. The other {trap}denies the truth when it reaches him{/trap}. The first fabricates, the second disbelieves. The verse warns of where that path ends.
now: Someone in the family chat forwards a message: share this or Allah will punish you. A friend says confidently what Allah thinks of a person. {trap}Putting words in Allah's mouth is easy and feels pious.{/trap} {idea}Saying I do not know, Allah knows best, is the safer honesty.{/idea}
old: I am sure this is what Allah wants, so I can say it.
new: Claiming to speak for Allah is serious. I only say what I truly know.
try: Before forwarding any religious message today, check where it comes from. If unsure, do not send it.

title: Strive for Him, and He opens the paths.
subtitle: The surah of trials ends with a promise

row.title: guides
sub: to what you did not know

then: A surah that began with trials for the Makkan believers ends here. Ibn Kathir says it refers to the Prophet ﷺ, his Companions, and all who follow them. One early scholar explained: {idea}those who act on what they know, Allah guides to what they do not know.{/idea} And {reward}Allah is with those who do good.{/reward}
now: You want to pray better but do not know where to start. You want to understand the Quran but it feels too big. {trap}You wait until you have a full plan.{/trap} {idea}Do the one thing you already know{/idea}, today. The next step shows itself once you are walking.
old: I will start when I know exactly how.
